text: This trend is likely to continue as Singapore’s population and economy grow.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: If we do not adopt technology but continue to manage waste the way we do today, we will need a proportionate increase in manpower which we cannot meet without turning to more foreign labour, given our manpower constraints.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We know that Singapore’s workforce is shrinking and ageing.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Manpower costs across all sectors will continue to rise.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The challenge is even more acute in the ES industry, which many Singaporeans, as I had noted earlier, perceive as dirty and unappealing, and shun away from.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We might not be able to find workers, even if we were willing to pay for them.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Members would agree with me that increasing our reliance on foreign workers to collect waste is not a sustainable solution.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, we need to start putting in place systems now, such as the PWCS to automate waste collection, which will allow our workers in the ES industry to take on higher value-added jobs.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: From our recent consultations with industry players, the operating costs for PWCS comprise only a very small proportion of the total maintenance expenses for a condominium.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Hence, the PWCS will not significantly affect the residents’ maintenance fees.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Condominiums with PWCS will also benefit from reduced pests and odour, and manpower savings from not needing to manually transport waste within the premises.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: At the district level, premises will also enjoy more cost savings due to economies of scale through shared bin centres, air and ventilation equipment, and pipe networks.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In greenfield sites, these benefits would be even greater, as the planning and construction of the network will be done from the start without retrofitting.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This is seen in other cities, including several in South Korea, where DPWCS are implemented on greenfield sites.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Over the longer term, as PWCS is used more extensively in Singapore and with technological advancements, we can expect the cost of DPWCS to decrease.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As mentioned in my opening speech, NEA estimates that a 1,000 DU-unit condominium would save GFA equivalent to a 5-room HDB flat by eliminating its bin centre.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In Kampong Bugis, this translates to the Master Developer saving 20% of the GFA used for bin centres, which could then be diverted to saleable units or facilities for residents.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Residents will also benefit from a cleaner and quieter environment due to reduced truck traffic.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Mr Murali Pillai asked whether the Government would consider subsidising existing private developments to implement PWCS within their estates.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Currently, the costs of conveying waste from individual chutes to bin centres in private developments are borne by residents through their monthly maintenance fees.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, the Government does not subsidise this and we have no plans to do so.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Mr Murali Pillai and Mr Zainal Sapari spoke about operational concerns related to DPWCS in Singapore and other cities, such as suction noise and smell from choked pipes.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: PWCS itself is a tried and tested technology and has been used in countries, such as South Korea and Sweden, for many years.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: To date, some 140 condominiums and commercial developments in Singapore have also used PWCS with only minor operational issues.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Where disamenities occur, we will study and address them.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For example, chokages have been addressed by improving the design of refuse chute hoppers, and odour, by ensuring the regular replacement of odour filters.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Residents were initially concerned when they saw the shared bin centre in the middle of the district.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: They were concerned that the bin centre would affect the aesthetics of the area, and whether there would be odour problems.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: These concerns were cleverly addressed by integrating the bin centre into a landscape garden, which residents welcomed.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The PWCS retrofitting project at Yuhua faced design limitations as it was in an existing estate with limited space.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As a result, the bin centre had to be located in the middle of the estate, surrounded by blocks of flats.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: HDB has introduced acoustic mitigating measures and odour treatment solutions to address the noise and smell issues at the bin centre.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Public education efforts were also intensified to remind residents of items that cannot be disposed of in the PWCS.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This would prevent chokages that give rise to odours.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: More importantly, the learning points from Yuhua have been incorporated into the Government's upcoming projects.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: These include the PWCS at the new HDB estate at Tampines North, where the bin centre will be located at the edge of the district, away from residents.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Other effective design features include placing refuse hoppers outside of flats and sizing refuse hoppers to limit the size of items that can be thrown into the chute, thereby preventing chokage.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: New developments, such as those in Kampong Bugis, will incorporate such planning and design features that will facilitate the smooth operation of the PWCS.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Another cause of disamenities is improper maintenance of the PWCS.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: PWCS vendors must also provide operation and maintenance manuals to managing agents and MCSTs and provide basic training to the staff of the managing agents.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As Ms Irene Quay, Mr Gan Thiam Poh and Dr Chia Shi Lu highlighted, users of DPWCS have a role to play in preventing chokage and its associated issues.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: They must use the DPWCS correctly and avoid throwing bulky or long items, such as pillows or brooms into the chutes.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: NEA will support such efforts to educate residents on the correct way to use the PWCS, as we are already doing at private developments which have adopted PWCS.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For instance, signage could be placed at throw-points to educate residents on proper usage.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: NEA has also amended the Code of Practice on Environmental Health to introduce a refuse chute hopper design that limits the size of items that can be thrown into the chute.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In the event of a prolonged disruption in the main DPWCS network, the licensee must ensure continued service, such as through manual waste collection.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: These contingency plans are similar to those in other countries, such as South Korea.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: PWCSs are also equipped with sensors and monitors to alert operators of any system faults so that they can carry out prompt remediation.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Even as we prepare for contingencies, it is pertinent to note that most chokages are cleared within two to three hours in existing developments that use PWCS in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Mr Murali Pillai, Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Louis Ng spoke about the Town Councils' role in managing PWCS.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Mr Murali Pillai and Ms Sylvia Lim also asked why the Bill excludes Town Council-managed premises.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This is because HDB has already been playing an active role in implementing PWCS in public housing estates.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Hence, the current Bill focuses on enabling DPWCS to be implemented on sites comprising private developments.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: NEA and HDB are also collaborating closely on implementing PWCS and will be adopting the Singapore Standard for PWCS in the new projects.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Mr Louis Ng spoke about potential increases in maintenance costs to Town Councils due to PWCS.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: While this Bill covers private developments only, we understand that HDB works closely with Town Councils to address this.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In addition, Town Councils will enjoy savings from PWCS due to the reduced manpower requirements for refuse collection and cleaning.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Indeed, they are already seeing this but in the initial phases, because the PWCS is only applied to a particular part of the constituency, the savings in collection costs cannot be passed through directly and, therefore, the temporary grant is given.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Whereas in a private development, the costs can be directly offset in the maintenance fees payable.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We welcome Mr Murali Pillai's suggestion to extend the scope of DPWCS, by combining public and private estates to allow for greater economies of scale.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This is something we can explore in future after we gain more experience in implementing DPWCS.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Ms Sylvia Lim asked how we intend to roll out the DPWCS areas under section 31G.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Our plan is to implement the DPWCS at Kampong Bugis, a greenfield development site that will enable the DPWCS to be planned and integrated from inception.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We currently have no plans for a nation-wide rollout of the DPWCS to existing developments or brownfield sites.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Our priority is to implement the Kampong Bugis DPWCS well and ensure that it operates smoothly.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Ms Sylvia Lim also asked about extending to landed estates.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: One of our considerations in implementing DPWCS is the financial viability and sustainability of the system.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will focus our efforts on non-landed developments, such as Kampong Bugis.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will work with the planning agencies to identify suitable areas and take into account not just the site and technical feasibility but also cost considerations.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will only implement DPWCS if it makes sense, if it benefits the residents.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, I want to assure everyone that we are not going to impose DPWCS in all developments.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: It will be judiciously done and costs will be a key consideration.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The composition has remained stable over the past three years.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The Tripartite Cluster for Cleaners (TCC) has been rallying all stakeholders to support measures to uplift the skills and wages of cleaners, including the PWM Bonus.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: To raise awareness among workers, a need highlighted by Mr Desmond Choo, the unions have been conducting roadshows and briefings and have reached out to more than 6,500 workers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: More sessions are being planned, and cleaning businesses have also been reminded to inform their workers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Thanks to the TCC's efforts, some cleaning businesses have already factored in the PWM Bonus in their contracts that extend beyond 2019.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Others, such as 800 Super Holdings Limited, have also been giving out additional bonuses to motivate and appreciate their workers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Indeed, I hope more businesses will do the same.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I also support Mr Zainal Sapari's heartfelt call for service buyers to safeguard the welfare of their cleaners.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Several Members asked how the PWM Bonus will be enforced, and how errant businesses would be flagged out.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: NEA and MOM routinely inspect the records of cleaning businesses to ensure compliance with the PWM requirements.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This includes making sure payslips are issued and training records of cleaners are kept.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Mr Murali Pillai was concerned how existing cleaning contracts will be affected and what considerations the Director-General of Public Health will take into account before invoking the powers to postpone the effective date of the PWM wage requirements.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Mr Zainal Sapari also suggested giving a grace period for businesses which do not pay the PWM Bonus when the requirement takes effect.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The TCC had consulted service buyers and providers extensively and deliberately recommended that the PWM Bonus be implemented only in 2020.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This was to give cleaning businesses ample time of more than three years to adjust their service agreements accordingly.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As such, all cleaning businesses will be required to pay their resident cleaners PWM Bonus from January 2020.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For cases of non-compliance, NEA will review their circumstances on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Mr Louis Ng raised concerns about cleaners' wages being reset when a contract ends and there is a change in service provider.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The TCC shares such concerns and had, therefore, proposed the yearly PWM wage increments, which would steadily lift wages at all skills levels for cleaners entering into contracts after 1 July 2018.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We urge cleaning businesses and service buyers to recognise the skills and experience of workers and pay them fairly.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: By investing in productivity enhancements and technology, businesses can afford to sustain higher wages for their workers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The Government will continue to support cleaning businesses in pursuing productivity projects through various schemes, such as the ES Productivity Solutions Grant (ES PSG).

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Under the ES PSG, cleaning businesses can receive support for up to half the cost of eligible productivity enhancement solutions, up to a maximum of $250,000.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Service buyers should also reject cheap-sourcing in favour of performance-based contracting.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This will encourage cleaning companies to invest in productivity measures without compromising the interest of cleaners, a concern highlighted by Mr Desmond Choo.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Besides ensuring fair wages, we need to help our cleaners upskill and keep up with industry demands.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Ms Joan Pereira asked whether training is tailored to the needs of all cleaners.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: All cleaners attend a basic cleaning course before starting out.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The courses are offered in various languages, including English, Mandarin and Malay.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: To facilitate learning, courses are designed to emphasise hands-on learning, which is best suited for the profile of the workers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Cleaners continue to receive support after they start work.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For example, Horsburgh Integrated Services groups new and experienced cleaners together to facilitate on-the-job training.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Another example is Lifeline Cleaning Pte Ltd, where older workers comprise 80% of the staff.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The company tapped the WorkPro Job Redesign Grant and successfully trained its cleaners to use machines to clean floors more efficiently.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In fact, I recently met 67-year-old Mr Lee Thian Kok from Lifeline, who has learnt to operate automated cleaning devices that make his job easier and more productive.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Mr Lee exemplifies the spirit of lifelong learning and is proof that older cleaners are not disadvantaged.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will support workers of all ages to upskill and reskill and encourage more businesses to adopt these best practices.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Cleaning work must not only become more efficient; it must also become safer.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Dr Chia Shi-Lu highlighted the need for tighter safety measures to protect cleaners at work.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Mr Louis Ng suggested extending PWM beyond the current pool of cleaners, to cleaners who are directly employed as well as foreign workers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: PWM was designed to help cleaners employed by cleaning businesses earn higher incomes through upskilling.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Previously, these workers saw their wages depressed as cheap-sourcing was prevalent across the industry.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: PWM sought to level the playing field, amidst a more comprehensive effort to raise wages of lower-income citizens across the board.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: While PWM does not apply to cleaners who are directly employed, we urge employers who are doing well to share their gains and reward their workers fairly, adopting the key principles of PWM.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Foreign workers are hired on different terms, and employers already bear other related expenses, such as additional levies and accommodation arrangements, for engaging them.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: While PWM does not apply to the foreign workers, again, we encourage employers to adopt the key principles of progressive wages when paying their foreign cleaners.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Regarding Mr Louis Ng's suggestions to adopt the R1 scheme for foreign workers in the cleaning sector, there is already such a scheme for the services sector which covers cleaning businesses.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Under this scheme, employers enjoy lower levies and longer employment periods when they train and retain their foreign cleaners.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As for Dr Intan Mokhtar's suggestion of extending PWM to the F&B industry, I will convey it to my MOM colleagues to consider.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: With regard to Mr Chen Show Mao's comments, I would like to clarify that PWM is not a national minimum wage, but a framework to raise wages in tandem with productivity improvements.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: It is applied to selected sectors prone to cheap sourcing, wage stagnation and market failure, such as the cleaning sector, the lift sector that Mr Chen Show Mao talked about, and the security and landscaping sectors where wages are lower.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Dr Intan Mokhtar also asked for stronger enforcement action against motorists who litter and cause roadside fires.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The Committee also recommends that higher penalties be imposed for causing fires by littering of materials that contain embers, such as cigarette butts.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Regarding Dr Intan’s suggestion to deploy more surveillance cameras to tackle high-rise littering, NEA has deployed such cameras through our service providers more than 5,500 times over the past five years resulting in more than 5,000 enforcement actions.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will continue to be vigilant in tackling this issue, while also working with the community to foster collective responsibility and ownership of our shared spaces.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Dr Intan Mokhtar asked whether make-shift rubbish bins placed by good Samaritans to collect rubbish during community events or private functions would contravene section 17 of the Act.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Section 17 is not intended to discourage such activities.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We want to recognise our cleaners who have played such a big part in keeping Singapore clean and green.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As Mr Zainal Sapari said, there are many ways each of us can show our appreciation to the cleaners around us – by being considerate in the way we use public spaces, by picking up after ourselves, and by saying "thank you" to them.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: More importantly, as Dr Intan Mokhtar has emphasised, the onus is on each and every one of us to keep our housing estates clean.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah has shown the way with the Nee Soon "No Cleaners Day".

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We must build a city that is truly clean because Singaporeans are gracious and mindful of their community and the environment.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: At the same time, we will upskill our ES workers and improve their livelihood and working conditions.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: All Singaporeans will benefit as we ensure a cleaner and greener environment in the years to come.
